Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement security intake for MedSys Health (closing the integration in June) our security and audits teams asked for a consolidated SIG/CAIQ response plus a short justification/categorization of any contractor subprocessors that have cryptographic key access or KMS access paths.

High level asks:
- A single consolidated SIG/CAIQ pack or spreadsheet showing our answers and evidence pointers (we accept a Drive link).
- A CSV roster of subprocessors that shows which ones are contractors (vendor classification), whether they have crypto/KMS access, and where keys are provisioned (Redwood KMS, customer-managed KMS, ephemeral).
- Any short blurb about mitigations (separation of duties, ephemeral creds, telemetry).

Can you get a consolidated bundle by end of this week (Friday 29th)? If not, a roadmap with dates would work. I can loop in our audits ops if you want to pre-validate.

Thanks,

Jamie Long
Head of Integrations Security
MedSys Health

Jamie —

Thanks for the clear asks. We can provide a consolidated SIG/CAIQ export and the subprocessor roster with the crypto column. Quick clarifications so we scope correctly:

1) Contractor definition: do you want us to flag everyone listed as "contractor" in our HR/vendor system, or only third-party vendors engaged via short-term SOWs? We typically classify "contractor" for both internal contingent staff and vendor contractors — we'll follow your preference.

2) KMS access types: we will enumerate (a) Redwood-managed KMS, (b) customer-managed KMS (if configured), (c) ephemeral keying (EPHEMERAL tokens/KV cache only). Is that level of granularity sufficient?

Plan:
- Ben will pull the subprocessor CSV and annotate the contractor flag and crypto access column (ETA: Wed EOD).
- I'll produce a SIG/CAIQ consolidated doc with evidence pointers and a short notes doc describing our crypto boundary for contractors (ETA: Thu).
- Marissa will assemble a single archive with quick-read executive blurb and evidence files (ETA: Fri morning).

If that timeline works I'll proceed and share the Drive folder.

Karthik
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Marissa —

I've pulled the current subprocessor export and annotated the contractor flag per the vendor system (we flagged contingent workforce + short-term SOW vendors as "contractor"). Summary highlights included in the CSV:

- Total subprocessors: 72
- Marked as contractors: 11
- Of those 11, 3 have any form of crypto/KMS access:
  * KeyBroker (ephemeral wrap for model checkpoints) — access via ephemeral provisioning, keys in Redwood-managed KMS, no long-term access.
  * EdgeTrust (onboarding contractor for telemetry) — limited signing token access, no KMS private key operations; credentials are rotated daily.
  * LightningOps (ops contractor supporting on-prem customer installs) — has admin-level access to customer-managed KMS when customers enable private deployment; otherwise no generic KMS access.

I also compiled a short provenance doc (kms-provenance-summary.pdf) that maps who can request key material and where keys are stored. For contractors our controls are: ephemeral credentials, scoped IAM roles, mandatory MFA, logging/tracing to our audit pipeline, and automation-controlled key rotation.

I've attached the annotated CSV excerpt in the Drive folder and uploaded the provenance summary.

Ben
Vendor Risk Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms-provenance-summary.pdf
